Regarding the definition of "zero-shot generalization" in the context of text-to-image AIs, it seems sensible. The concept of zero-shot generalization refers to the ability of a model to apply its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts without requiring additional training data. In the context of text-to-image AIs, this means that the model can generate images based on text prompts without having seen the specific images or concepts before.

The 2013 paper cited in the response likely discussed the concept of zero-shot generalization in the context of deep learning and neural networks, and how it applies to text-to-image AIs. The definition of zero-shot generalization is indeed relevant to text-to-image AIs, as it highlights the model's ability to generalize knowledge learned from a specific dataset to new, unseen concepts.

It's worth noting that zero-shot generalization is a challenging task, especially in the context of text-to-image AIs, where the model needs to generate images that are not only visually plausible but also semantically coherent with the text prompt. However, recent advances in deep learning and neural networks have made significant progress in achieving zero-shot generalization in text-to-image AIs, and this concept continues to be an active area of research in the field.
